extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: The CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets are labeled subsets of the 80 million tiny images dataset. CIFAR-10 consists of 6,000 32x32 colour images in each of 10 mutually exclusive classes (50,000 training images and 10,000 test images). CIFAR-100 consists of 600 images in each of 100 non-overlapping classes grouped into 20 superclasses.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.citeAs: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images. Technical Report, University of Toronto.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The underlying 80 million tiny images dataset was collected by searching the web for every non-abstract English noun in WordNet using search engines including Google, Flickr, and Altavista, keeping roughly the first 3,000 results per search term. For CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, student annotators examined the search results for each class and its WordNet hyponyms to filter out mislabeled images based on specific inclusion criteria.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the web collected via search engines (Google, Flickr, Altavista) using WordNet nouns as search terms.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: over the span of six months
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32. In the raw dataset, perfect duplicates and images where an excessively large portion of pixels were white were removed. In the labeled subset, duplicate images and re-saved JPEGs were removed by comparing images using the L2 norm with a liberal rejection threshold. For modeling experiments, ZCA whitening was applied and the 1,000 least significant principal components of variance were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Student annotators were paid a fixed hourly rate to inspect candidate images corresponding to a class name and its WordNet hyponyms, filtering out mislabeled examples. Annotators were instructed to accept images if the category name was a likely answer to 'What is in this picture?', ensure images were photorealistic (rejecting line drawings and cartoons), include only images with one prominent instance of the object (unless the class name was plural), and accept partially occluded objects or unusual viewpoints if identifiable. All labels submitted by the annotators were personally verified by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All labels submitted by labelers were personally verified by the researchers to ensure consistency and correctness.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Students paid a fixed sum per hour spent labeling.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The images tend to exhibit symmetry about the horizontal and vertical axes, likely caused by human photographic bias (centering the main object and keeping the ground plane horizontal).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The original tiny images web search labels are extremely unreliable. Large models trained on the data exhibited a strong tendency to overfit without proper regularization or pre-training.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Object recognition, image classification, unsupervised feature learning, and evaluating generative and feed-forward models such as RBMs, DBNs, and neural networks.
